title: Add or subtract the equations to target one value
subtitle: Systems of two linear equations in two variables · 23 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **23 of the official questions in Systems of two linear equations in two variables are this one** — 3 Easy, 13 Medium, 7 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You get two equations in standard form.
- One variable has opposite (or equal) coefficients in the two equations, or the target is an expression like x + y or 2x − y rather than a single variable.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Before you solve anything, check whether adding or subtracting the equations as they stand cancels the variable you do not need, or produces the target expression.
- You don't need to find the other variable at all.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Works as a fallback: graph both equations, read the intersection, then calculate the requested expression from the coordinates.
Adding the equations is usually faster than typing them.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You fully solve the system and then give the value of the wrong variable.
The choices include the other variable's value and a partial result on purpose.
Watch negative signs when you subtract.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You fully solve the system and then give the value of the wrong variable.
The choices include the other variable's value and a partial result on purpose.
